verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's RTX developer docs cover the low-precision half of the story: fifth-gen Tensor Cores with FP4 and FP8, plus an FP8 Transformer Engine for LLM inference in TensorFlow and PyTorch. Community reports confirm FP4 matters and that llama.cpp has been benchmarked on the 5090. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of supported serving stacks for this part (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, llama.cpp), any 5090-specific inference guide, and independent confirmation of FP4/FP8 serving in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, this GPU has a documented LLM inference story — low-precision formats (FP8/FP4) and supported serving stacks (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, ROCm, llama.cpp) for this part

citations.quote: Fifth-generation Tensor Cores deliver up to 3x higher throughput for deep learning, with new FP4 support for massive performance gains alongside TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, and FP6 precision.
A second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine... accelerates LLM prototyping, inference, and AI development across frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch.
Summary from a commenter on Llama.cpp benchmarks: performance isn't bad, but perf per watt isn't better than the 4080 or 4090.
